original_question: Is the Bergman metric complete on bounded pseudoconvex domains whose boundary regularity is less than C^1?
target_in_paper: Theorem 1.2: "The Bergman metric of any bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary is complete."
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the core topic: Bergman-metric completeness for bounded pseudoconvex domains when one weakens the previously known C^1-boundary hypothesis. It is also faithful to the paper’s motivation, since §1 explicitly recalls Ohsawa’s C^1 result before turning to a weaker boundary assumption.
missing_details: The paper does not ask about an arbitrary class of boundaries "less than C^1"; the precise weaker regularity treated is Lipschitz boundary.
The ambient setting is a bounded domain D ⊂ ℂ^n, with n arbitrary.
Completeness means completeness with respect to the Bergman metric ds_D^2 associated to the Bergman kernel K_D(z,w).
The paper’s stronger main criterion is Theorem 1.1: local condition S implies Bergman completeness; Theorem 1.2 is the Lipschitz-boundary corollary of that criterion.
Your draft risks conflating this precise Lipschitz result with Kobayashi’s broader question, also quoted in §1, asking which bounded pseudoconvex domains in ℂ^n are Bergman complete.
The nearby Theorem 1.3 is a different hyperconvex/symmetric-Green-function criterion and should not be folded into the boundary-regularity version of the question.
refined_question: Let D ⊂ ℂ^n be a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary. Must D be complete with respect to its Bergman metric ds_D^2?
justification: The draft is closest to the paper’s boundary-regularity corollary, not to the broader Kobayashi question and not to the separate hyperconvex criterion of Theorem 1.3. In §1 the author recalls that Ohsawa proved Bergman completeness for pseudoconvex domains with C^1 boundary, then states the stronger local condition-S theorem (Theorem 1.1) and immediately specializes it to Theorem 1.2 for bounded pseudoconvex domains with Lipschitz boundary. Section 3 supplies the missing bridge by proving that a bounded pseudoconvex domain with Lipschitz boundary locally satisfies condition S, so the paper’s exact boundary-regularity formulation is Lipschitz, not an unspecified class of regularities weaker than C^1.

citations.label: unnumbered concluding argument deriving Theorem 1.2 from Theorem 1.1 via local condition S
